Single-server release. Published experimental pair.

The earlier 0.1.0-alpha2 APK installs one-server IKEv2. The experimental 0.2.0-alpha2 prerelease installs IKEv2 → AmneziaWG across two distinct VPSs. Reviewed phone reset, role swapping and an optional SSH management relay are implemented. Other phone engines remain proposals. The earlier 0.1.0-alpha2 download is single-server.

One route works today.

Rookstride deploys strongSwan, AdGuard Home and Unbound on one fresh VPS, manages access over pinned SSH, and connects through its embedded IKEv2 engine. That remains the small starting point.

IMPLEMENTED / EXPERIMENTAL

Two bridges.
One journey.

Choose an entry and an exit. The phone installs each through its own verified SSH connection. After setup, the servers forward the traffic; the phone does not have to keep an administration connection open.

  1. 01

    Your phone

    Existing IKEv2 engine

  2. 02

    Entry VPS

    strongSwan → AWG 3.1

  3. 03

    Exit VPS

    AdGuard → Unbound
    IPv4 Internet exit

The Two-Hop VPN Gateway scripts now underpin the experimental app adapter, with independent SSH identities, durable per-node jobs and blocked failure recovery.

The first implemented combination is IKEv2 → AmneziaWG 3.1. It uses Rookstride’s existing phone engine. AdGuard Home and Unbound run on the exit. Read the pair installation and recovery guide.

Changing the connection between the servers does not change IKEv2 between your phone and the entry. A blocked first-hop connection needs a reachable endpoint and an appropriate phone-facing protocol.

Choose a tested recipe.

strongSwan implements IKEv2. AmneziaVPN is an app that offers several protocols. OpenVPN, WireGuard, AmneziaWG and Xray each need their own integration; a dropdown cannot make the existing IKEv2 engine speak all of them.

Xray / VLESS / REALITYProxy engine + full-device TUN integrationSingle first; backhaul laterResearch / not in APK

WireGuard/AWG and OpenVPN provide routable tunnel interfaces. Xray is a proxy engine: full-device routing also requires TUN, DNS, UDP and IPv6 policy integration. Its transport choices have compatibility limits.

Deploying a server, exporting its configuration, and connecting inside Rookstride are separate milestones. External-client export can come first; the goal is integrated connection after each engine passes its tests.

Android permits one active VPN service per user/profile. Two-hop happens on the servers, rather than starting two VPNs on the phone. Additional engines also increase APK size and maintenance; the existing Android 8 IKEv2 path should stay available.

Open the far bridge first.

  1. Pick one server or two. Choose a supported recipe and enter each host’s independent SSH port, administrator and credentials.
  2. Verify both identities. Pin host fingerprints; inspect OS, architecture, kernel support, existing services and non-overlapping address ranges.
  3. Prepare the exit. Install DNS and Internet egress before opening client forwarding on the entry.
  4. Join and check. Establish the backhaul. Verify exit IPv4, DNS and return routing with a staged source.
  5. Activate the route. Connect from a real device and check the complete path. If a step fails, forwarding stays blocked.
  6. Resume safely. A per-server job journal survives a dropped phone connection; inspect partial state before repeating any destructive step.

The mobile coordinator uses independent SSH users/ports, strict key verification and private temporary files. Pause keeps a persistent forwarding guard and blackhole route. Owned interrupted jobs can resume. Review both nodes and type DELETE PAIR to reset their owned VPN data, then swap entry and exit and reinstall. Ubuntu, SSH and unrelated files remain. Pair upgrades and importing arbitrary existing pairs remain future work.

A pair earns its own proof.

The earlier three signed-APK cycles tested a single-server IKEv2 gateway. They do not establish two-hop or another protocol’s behavior.

The same signed 0.2.0-alpha2 APK repeatedly configured both nodes on independent providers, with managed phone resets between runs and reversed roles. Embedded Android and isolated provider-side Linux clients verified real IKE/EAP, exit IPv4, ad DNS and bridge stop/recovery. Phone-process interruption and both-node reboot recovery passed. Android 16’s coordinator and VPN passed; screen navigation remains incomplete because of System UI startup hangs. Physical/OEM phones, real IPv6 handoff, sustained load and native 16-KiB runtime remain gates.

Read the provider test report and machine-readable evidence. One return path from this computer lost UDP replies to node A; a provider-side client reached A successfully. The report identifies each client network. Historical local alpha1 evidence remains available.

More hops do not guarantee anonymity, fix a website’s exit-IP restrictions, or hide GPS, account and cookie signals. They add another provider, cost and failure point.
